titulo: Uterus: phases of the menstrual cycle
descricao_original: The four phases of the menstrual cycle are shown here at the same magnification to demonstrate both glandular changes and variation in thickness of the endometrium during the menstrual cycle. 10x

bases.legenda_ia: Imagem-base educacional de histologia da pagina 'Uterus: phases of the menstrual cycle', no setor Órgãos e Sistemas > Sistema Reprodutor > Feminino > Uterus > Uterus 17. Descricao original da pagina: The four phases of the menstrual cycle are shown here at the same magnification to demonstrate both glandular changes and variation in thickness of the endometrium during the menstrual cycle. 10x. Este arquivo nao contem os marcadores interativos; use as camadas PNG relacionadas para localizar estruturas. Origem: Digital Histology, https://digitalhistology.org/organs-systems/reproductive/female/uterus/uterus-17/, acesso em 2026-08-07.

marcadores.explicacao_original: (days 6-14) The proliferative phase (days 6-14) shows straight glands with no secretory product in the lumens, no evidence of spiral arteries, and a relatively thin endometrium.
marcadores.legenda_ia: Camada transparente de anotacao da pagina 'Uterus: phases of the menstrual cycle'. Deve ser sobreposta, sem redimensionamento independente, a 'O.R.F.U.17.jpg'. Destaca a estrutura ou conceito 'Proliferative phase' por setas, contornos ou marcadores coloridos (incluindo vermelho quando presente). Explicacao original: (days 6-14) The proliferative phase (days 6-14) shows straight glands with no secretory product in the lumens, no evidence of spiral arteries, and a relatively thin endometrium.. marcadores.explicacao_original: (days 15-25) Endometrium in the secretory phase (days 15-25) reaches maximal thickness. Spiral arteries are readily identifiable; glands become secretory. Predecidual cells appear around day 24.

marcadores.explicacao_original: (days 26-28) During the pre-menstrual phase (ischemic portion of the secretory phase, days 26-28), the endometrium shrinks and necrotic tissue is obvious. Other characteristics of the secretory phase continue.
